in_text_mentions: arynx staged at ​​cT4N2cM0. The patient underwent a total laryngopharyngectomy, bilateral neck dissections, and a free flap reconstruction. Pathology from the surgery showed a 5.5 cm tumor centered in the arytenoepiglottic fold, extending to the right pyriform sinus, bilateral posterior pharynx, bilateral hypopharynx, and right upper esophageal mucosa and muscularis propria. The mass abutted the thyroid cartilage, and both lymphovascular and perineural invasion were identified; only one lymph node was negative for metastatic carcinoma. Histology determined a squamous cell carcinoma (Figure 1).

in_text_mentions: Evaluation with flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy revealed a mass at the right pharyngeal wall extending to the right pyriform sinus (Figure 2). Ultrasound‐guided needle biopsy was attempted twice revealing acute inflammation and keratinized squamous cell epithelium of the right piriform sinus, respectively. Biopsy of the right level II lymph node showed chronic lymphocytic leukemia. A biopsy of the right piriform sinus under general anesthesia was then completed revealing well‐differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma.

plate_findings.evidence: H&E stained sections (100x) show bone with infiltrating squamous cells forming sheets and nests

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E section of a vertebral biopsy showing infiltrating squamous cell carcinoma nests in bone, stated in text to be compatible with the patient's known hypopharyngeal primary (positive CK5/6 and p40), so it is a specific histologic manifestation of hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. B: H&E section demonstrating keratin pearl formation and pleomorphic squamous cells infiltrating bone, consistent with metastatic hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma as stated in the text. C: p40 immunohistochemistry showing positive nuclear staining in the metastatic squamous cell carcinoma deposits, supporting squamous differentiation of the hypopharyngeal primary. D: Cytokeratin 5/6 immunohistochemistry with strong positive staining in the metastatic carcinoma deposits, corroborating squamous differentiation of the hypopharyngeal primary.

in_text_mentions: ging revealed an asymmetric soft tissue prominence at the larynx with thickening along the adjacent right hypopharynx, a 1.3 cm lymph node and fat stranding at the right carotid space. Laryngopharyngitis was diagnosed based on repeat examination and review of imaging. A primary care physician then obtained a noncontrast MRI for new headaches incidentally identifying a transglottic mass invading thyroid cartilage with encasement of the right carotid, and a 1.6 cm right level IIA lymph node (Figure 1). The patient was referred to our tertiary care center for concern of hypopharyngeal malignancy.

The caption and in-text report this as an isolated recurrence/metastasis of hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (final pathology consistent with metastatic hypopharyngeal carcinoma), so the panel depicts a specific, documented manifestation of the configured disease. It is an atypical/uncommon presentation (isolated PEG-site metastasis), and no skin, age or ethnicity information is provided in the caption or text.

plate_findings.evidence: Histopathological findings for hypopharyngeal tumor biopsy. Features observed include increased nuclear chromatin, disparity between large and small nuclei, and signs of mitosis. These findings are indicative of squamous cell carcinoma.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Low-power H&E section of the hypopharyngeal biopsy shows nests and sheets of atypical squamous epithelial cells with hyperchromatic, pleomorphic nuclei and mitotic activity embedded in stroma, matching the caption's diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx. b: Higher-magnification H&E view of the same hypopharyngeal biopsy showing a cohesive nest of malignant squamous cells with large hyperchromatic nuclei, prominent nucleoli and intervening inflammatory stroma, consistent with invasive squamous cell carcinoma.
